key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted that the second FIR lodged at Udaipur contained the same allegations as the first FIR at Hisar and additionally stated that the complainant had earlier lodged a complaint at Hisar.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, noting that the prosecution examined several police witnesses who proved police papers and documents relating to the marriage, but the complainant and victim did not appear before the court, leading to the acquittal of the appellant.
post_offence_conduct: The complainant and respondent wife neither appeared before the Trial Court at Hisar nor withdrew their complaint, showing their intention to harass the appellant by first making him face a trial in Hisar and then again at Udaipur.
bail_history: The appellant had been arrested and thereafter granted bail.

investigation_status: FIR No. 156 of 2015, Women Police Station, Udaipur was quashed by the Supreme Court. The investigation was stayed by the Supreme Court until further orders.
procedural_irregularity: The High Court erred in not quashing the FIR under Section 482 Cr.P.C. due to the abuse of process of law and the complainant's conduct of not withdrawing the first complaint or transferring it to Udaipur.

appeal_history.high_court: The High Court dismissed the quashing petition of the Appellant on the ground that the complaint in Udaipur was prior in point of time than the complaint in Hisar.
appeal_history.supreme_court: The appeal was allowed, and the impugned proceeding passed by the High Court was quashed.

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the High Court erred in not quashing the FIR under Section 482 Cr.P.C. as the second FIR was on the same set of allegations made by the complainant after the first FIR was lodged, constituting an abuse of process of law.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the High Court correctly dismissed the quashing petition, as the complaint in Udaipur was prior in point of time than the complaint in Hisar and the Rajasthan Police was unaware of the earlier proceedings.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that the abuse of process of law occurs when a complainant lodges a subsequent FIR on the same set of allegations without withdrawing the previous one, thereby misusing the state machinery for harassment.
precedent_relied_upon: Prem Chand Singh v. State of UP (2020) 3 SCC 54; T.T. Antony v. State of Kerala & Ors. [2001] 3 SCR 942; Y. Abraham Ajith & Ors. v. Inspector of Police, Chennai & Anr. [2004] Supp. 3 SCR 604
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed to quash the FIR and to deprecate the misuse of state machinery for harassment, with costs imposed on the respondent to compensate the appellant.
other_sentence_order: Compensation of Rs. 5,00,000/- to be deposited with the Registrar of the Supreme Court, with 50% transmitted to the Supreme Court Legal Services Committee and 50% to the appellant.
